## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The removed `--wait` option is a release-blocking break: scripts that pass `--wait` now fail at argument parsing, and the ADR this pull request adds says `--wait` stays accepted as an alias for one release.

## Changes
The pull request renames the CLI option `--wait` to `--timeout` in `app/cli.py` and updates the tests to match. It also adds ADR 007 describing the transition, plus a one-line `review.txt` file at the repository root.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — Keep `--wait` as a deprecated alias for `--timeout` — An existing invocation such as `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` now exits with status 2 ("unrecognized arguments"), because `--wait` is no longer registered. This contradicts `docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5`: "Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used." No test covers the alias or the warning. — Any user script or automation that passes `--wait` stops working on upgrade, with no deprecation period. — Fix: Register `--wait` with `dest="timeout"` and emit a `DeprecationWarning` when it is used, then add a `--wait` case to `test_explicit_options` and a test that asserts the warning.
